title: Introduce EMA-based fidelity prober and CI hysteresis autotuner
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an exponential-moving-average driven fidelity prober and a CI hysteresis autotuner to reduce noisy regression failures; includes docs and a migration guide for CI owners.
description: This PR adds a probabilistic fidelity prober that computes per-cohort exponential moving averages (EMA) of failure signals and uses a sensitivity-tierer to classify prompt-sets into stable/volatile tiers. The core goal is to reduce noisy CI failures from transient prompt flakiness while preserving fast detection of real regressions. The CI hysteresis autotuner adjusts gate thresholds and hold-times automatically based on recent EMA statistics and controlled cooldown windows. Highlights: 1) prober/agent: eval_harness/probers/ema_fidelity_prober.py - implements cohort EMA, smoothing, and probabilistic failure scoring; 2) sensitivity-tierer: eval_harness/metrics/sensitivity_tierer.py - maps cohorts into three tiers (stable/medium/volatile) and exposes config hooks for weighting; 3) CI hook: ci/hooks/ema_hysteresis_hook.yaml and ci/scripts/threshold_autotuner.py - integrates with GitHub Actions and the existing regression gate adapter; 4) repair suggester: tools/repair_suggester/README.md and repair_suggester/main.py - a lightweight heuristic that proposes prompt edits or alternate anchor examples when a cohort flips flakiness repeatedly; 5) docs: docs/ci/ema_fidelity_prober.md - operational guidance and rollout checklist. Motivation: teams running nightly prompt-set regressions see a high ratio of transient failures that create noisy alert fatigue and slow down rollouts. Existing static thresholds either cause frequent false positives or hide slow regressions. The EMA approach lets the system adapt to evolving baseline variance without losing sensitivity to sustained degradations. This change is backward compatible: default CI behavior is unchanged unless repo-level CI owners opt into the new hook. The PR includes a small synthetic benchmark harness used in local smoke runs to validate sensitivity tuning, and an optional gated canary flow that first applies the autotuner in shadow mode for a week before elevating it to enforcement. Implementation notes: - EMA window and smoothing alpha are configurable per-cohort in eval_harness/config/cohort_profiles.yaml. - Autotuner uses a conservative backoff policy and respects an explicit opt-out label (ci/no-autotune) for hotfixes. - Repair suggester emits a compact suggestion payload (YAML) that can be attached to PR build artifacts for triage. Security/Privacy: no production data is shipped; the prober operates on eval traces already produced by the harness. Backwards compatibility was confirmed by running the existing regression pipeline with the hooks disabled. Rolling deploy plan: - Merge to main in squash-merge. - Enable shadow mode via feature flag in repo CI for 7 days. - After monitoring (alerts for false suppression rate < 1%), flip to enforcement. Known limitations: - The autotuner requires a minimal baseline of historical traces (recommended 500 samples per cohort) to avoid excessive oscillation. - Repair suggestions are heuristic and intended as triage hints, not automatic edits. See docs for mitigation steps.

review_comments: Daniel Park: Nice approach. Two questions: (1) can you show a short chart in the docs comparing EMA vs fixed threshold on a noisy cohort? (2) is the repair suggester pluggable (we may want to call a separate annotator service)?
Maya Chen (author): Added a small synthetic chart to docs and made repair_suggester an interface with a simple local impl; added notes on how to swap in a networked annotator.
Priya Nair: CI integration looked good but I see the initial tests flaked in GH Actions. Can we make the integration test seed deterministic or mark as flaky?
Maya Chen: The integration test used randomized noise; I replaced it with a seeded RNG and added a CI-only env override to run a stressed variant. The GH Actions run now passes.
Liam O'Sullivan: Concern about oscillation on small cohorts. Could we add a minimum-sample guard to the autotuner?
Maya Chen: Added a guard (min_samples: 500) and explicit cooldown windows. Documented tradeoffs in the runbook.
Priya Nair: Approving pending docs clarifications on rollout.
ci_summary: Initial run: 3 flaky integration failures (seed sensitivity) -> fixed by deterministic seeding and reduced test parallelism; subsequent runs: all checks passed (unit tests, lint, mypy, regression-smoke). Performance lint flagged a minor N+1 in repair_suggester — addressed. Final status: pass.
merge_commit_message: Introduce EMA-based fidelity prober and CI hysteresis autotuner — adds adaptive gating and repair suggester (squash)
notes_for_release_manager: Feature is behind a repo-level CI flag. Recommend enabling in shadow mode for 7 days for each major repo. Communicate to SREs and platform teams. Ops playbook: docs/ci/ema_fidelity_prober.md
post_merge_actions: 1) Enable shadow mode via .github/ci_flags for targeted repos; 2) Run nightly synthetic benchmark for 3 days; 3) Monitor false suppression rate metric (eval.fidelity.false_suppression_rate)
qa_steps: Run tests in tests/probers/test_ema_prober.py and tests/ci/test_threshold_autotuner_integration.py locally; exercise shadow mode by setting env ENABLE_EMA_AUTO_TUNE=1 in CI; verify repair suggestions appear as schema-validated YAML artifacts.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Merge to main (squash). Stage 2: Enable shadow mode for a week on canary repos. Stage 3: Review metrics and opt-in by repo. Stage 4: Full enforcement after 7–14 days if false suppression < 1%.
observability_changes: Adds metrics: eval.ema.score, eval.ema.cohort_tier, eval.autotuner.threshold_adjustments, eval.repair_suggester.suggestions_emitted. Dashboards: docs/observability/ema_prober_dashboard.md
